transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me. 

Um... I guess the main reason I came in is just that I've been noticing I get pulled off track kind of easily? It's probably not a huge deal, but... well, like, if I get one Slack ping, or I hear a random song lyric, or even just get an idea for another project, suddenly I've totally lost the thread of the dashboard I was supposed to be finishing. 

I hope that makes sense? I just feel a little embarrassed about it, honestly, because I really do want to do a good job and be productive. I just get a bit sidetracked sometimes, if that's an okay thing to bring up here?
Have you noticed this tendency to get sidetracked throughout your life, even going back to when you were a child, or is this something that has started more recently?

Um... I guess, if I really think about it, it's kind of always been there? I hope I'm answering this right, but... even back in elementary school, my teachers would write comments on my report cards about it. They usually framed it nicely, but they did say I had a tendency to rush through my worksheets and, um, lose track of the directions. And I guess I sometimes talked over my classmates during group work? I always felt so bad about that when they brought it up, I just got really eager to share, you know? 

And at home... my parents were really sweet and they actually used to sit right beside me while I did my homework. Not because I couldn't understand the material or anything! Just because, well, I would kind of wander off or start a totally different activity before finishing the first one if they weren't there to keep me company. 

Is... is that the kind of childhood stuff you're asking about? I hope I'm not oversharing!
When you were younger, did you often find it difficult to stay seated in class or feel like you had an internal motor that kept you moving?

Um... I don't really think so? At least, I hope I wasn't too disruptive. I mean, I definitely liked to be active, like most kids, right? But I don't remember feeling like I couldn't stay in my seat or anything like that. 

I think I was mostly just... maybe a little wiggly sometimes? But I always tried really hard to follow the rules and stay where I was supposed to be. I don't think my teachers ever had to tell me to sit down a lot. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
In your day-to-day life now, do you often find yourself feeling restless or like you have a hard time waiting for your turn in conversations?

Um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I really try to be polite and listen when other people are talking, but... well, if I have to sit still through a really long Zoom call for one of my classes, or if I'm just supposed to quietly study in one spot for a while, I do start to feel... kind of an uncomfortable pressure? 

It's not a big deal, really! It's just this feeling in my body like I need to get up and pace around, or at least do something with my hands. I usually just try to doodle or fiddle with a pen so I don't bother anyone. I hope that doesn't make me sound too impatient or anything? I really do want to pay attention, it just gets a little hard to stay perfectly still sometimes. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
When you have a large project to complete, do you find it difficult to organize your tasks or keep track of all the steps needed to finish them?

Um... I wouldn't say I find it super difficult? I mean, I can definitely get things done! I usually try to make a list or something so I know what I'm supposed to do. 

Sometimes, I guess, if it's a really huge project with a ton of little moving parts, it can feel a tiny bit overwhelming at first? But I think that's pretty normal for college, right? Everyone gets a little stressed out by big assignments. I usually figure it out eventually, even if I have to kind of... jump around between different parts of the project instead of doing it perfectly in order. 

I hope that doesn't sound like I'm disorganized! I really do try my best to keep everything straight. Did I answer that okay?
Looking back over the past six months, how often would you say you have felt the need to get up and leave your seat or move around during situations where you are expected to remain still?

Um... over the past six months? I don't think it's been very often at all. I mean, I really try to be respectful of the rules and stay where I'm supposed to be, especially in my classes. 

I guess maybe... if a lecture is going on for a really, really long time, I might feel a tiny urge to stretch my legs? But I usually just try to shift in my chair or maybe bounce my foot a little so I don't distract anyone else. I wouldn't actually just get up and leave my seat unless we were on a break or something. 

I hope that's normal? I think everyone gets a little stiff sitting for too long, right? I really do try to be a good student and not cause any disruptions. Is that what you were asking?
In your daily life, do you often lose things that you need to get your work or other tasks done, like your keys, phone, or important documents?

Um... lose things? No, I don't think I do that very often. I mean, I'm pretty careful with my stuff, especially important things like my phone or my keys. 

I guess sometimes, maybe, I might misplace a pen or a notebook for a minute or two? Like, I'll set it down on my desk and then forget exactly which pile of papers I put it under. But I always find it right away! It's never anything major, and I always make sure I have what I need before I head to class. 

I think everyone misplaces little things sometimes, right? Especially when you're studying hard and have a lot on your mind. I really try to be responsible and keep track of my belongings. Does that make sense? I hope I don't sound careless!
In your daily interactions or class participation, do you frequently blurt out answers before a question has been completed or find it difficult to wait for your turn in group settings?

Um... blurt out answers? Oh, no, I really try not to do that. I know it's important to be polite and let people finish speaking, especially professors or other students in group projects. I try really hard to be a good listener. 

I mean, I guess sometimes... like, if we're doing check-ins at a hackathon or I'm waiting in line for office hours, I might get a tiny bit antsy? Just because I want to make sure I get my question answered and I know everyone is super busy. I might catch myself checking my watch a little or shifting around, and maybe... sometimes I feel a little eager to jump in and share my update before it's officially my turn? But I always try to catch myself and wait! I don't want to be rude or talk over anyone. 

It's just that I get so excited about the projects, you know? I think it's normal to feel a little impatient when you're really invested in your work, right? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad team member. I really do try to wait my turn. Did I explain that okay?
When you are working on your assignments or tasks, do you often find that you make careless mistakes because you didn't notice a small detail or didn't pay close enough attention?

Um... careless mistakes? I try really, really hard not to make them. I always want my work to look professional and show that I care about the class. 

I guess... well, occasionally, if I'm working on a project, like a mockup or a data chart for a class, I'll submit it thinking it's totally polished and perfect. But then... maybe later I'll notice that I, um, mislabeled an axis or used the wrong color key? Or maybe I missed a tiny little instruction in the project brief. 

It's never because I don't care, though! I just get really focused on the big picture of the design or the data, and sometimes those tiny details just slip by me. I always feel so bad when it happens, and I try to double-check everything. I think everyone overlooks a small detail every now and then when they're working on complex projects, right? I hope that doesn't mean I'm doing a bad job. I really do try my best to catch everything. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
In your daily life, do you find that you frequently forget to do routine tasks, like returning calls, keeping appointments, or completing daily chores?

Um... forgetting routine tasks? I really pride myself on being dependable, so I try my absolute best to stay on top of my schedule. I don't want anyone to think I'm ignoring them. 

I guess... well, occasionally, I might slip up with a few basic things? Like, if I'm doing a little freelance design work on the side, I might accidentally forget to return a client call right away, or send a quick follow-up email. Or, um, maybe I'll head out to an art meetup and realize I forgot to bring my sketchbook with me. 

But I really try to prevent that! I'm actually very proactive—I set multiple reminders on my phone for absolutely everything because I want to be super organized. It's just that sometimes... if I'm deep into studying or working, and a reminder pops up, I might just swipe it away. I always tell myself I'll do it the very second I finish what I'm doing, but then... I kind of forget again. 

I always feel so awful when that happens, because I really don't want to come across as flaky or lazy. I think it's pretty normal to accidentally dismiss a notification when you're super busy, don't you think? I really hope that doesn't make me sound irresponsible... I promise I try my hardest to keep track of it all. Does that make sense?
Do you find that these difficulties with focus and organization happen in multiple areas of your life, such as both at home and at school or work?

Um... multiple areas of my life? Oh, I really try to keep things separate and not let any stress bleed over into other parts of my day. I want to be someone who has it all together, you know? 

I guess... well, I wouldn't say it happens *everywhere*. Like, I try really hard to keep my dorm room neat, and I want my professors to see me as a dedicated student. I mean, maybe sometimes the little slip-ups I mentioned happen at school with my assignments, and then maybe... occasionally at home, like if I forget to do my laundry on the day I planned or I misplace my keys when I'm rushing out the door. 

But it's not like my whole life is a mess or anything! I really try to stay on top of things in both places. I think everyone has days where they're a little scattered at school and then come home and forget a chore, right? It's just normal college student stuff, I hope? I really do my best to manage it all so it doesn't affect my roommates or my grades. Did I answer that right?
